lines.text: Twenty three people. It's a coin flip that two share a birthday.
lines.caption: 23 people. It's a coin flip that two share a birthday.

lines.text: Three hundred sixty five days. Add people one by one.
lines.caption: 365 days. Add people one by one.

lines.text: Twelve percent sounds small, but count pairs. Twenty three people make two hundred fifty three pairs, each one a chance to match.
lines.caption: 12% sounds small, but count pairs. 23 people make 253 pairs, each one a chance to match.

lines.text: At twenty three people, the chance is fifty point seven percent.
lines.caption: At 23 people, the chance is 50.7%.

lines.text: At fifty people it's ninety seven percent. At seventy, ninety nine point nine percent.
lines.caption: At 50 people it's 97%. At 70, 99.9%.

lines.text: Careful: that's any two people. Matching your birthday takes two hundred fifty three others.
lines.caption: Careful: that's any two people. Matching YOUR birthday takes 253 others.

lines.text: Have you met your birthday twin? Tell us below.

post.title: 23 people, 50% chance: the birthday paradox
post.description: With 23 people, the chance that two share a birthday is 50.7%, because 23 people make 253 pairs. 50 people: 97%. 70 people: 99.9%. Assumes 365 equally likely days. Narrated with an AI voice. Animation made with code.
